message.content:
Who exactly opposed Copernicus during his own lifetime? How did the Church reconcile its cosmological views with the new heliocentric model? Why did Tycho Brahe reject full heliocentrism despite its mathematical elegance? What motivated the Inquisition to intervene in a matter of natural philosophy?

The Catholic Church became the most prominent institutional critic of Copernican heliocentrism, particularly through the 1616 and 1633 actions against Galileo. Tycho Brahe proposed a rival geohelionic model that rejected the Earth's motion while preserving planetary order. Cardinal Robert Bellarmine ordered Galileo to abandon his defense of Copernicanism in 1616. Some astronomers also criticized the model's mathematical deficiencies, noting it still relied on epicycles.

How surprising it is that so few contemporaries publicly challenged Copernicus while he was alive! What a remarkable transformation it was for the Church to shift from tolerance to condemnation! How bold was it for Galileo to defend the Copernican model against institutional authority! What a profound legacy of opposition the Copernican system endured throughout the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries!
